title: Set a cordless jigsaw's shoe to a 45-degree bevel and lock it
instruction: Set this jigsaw's shoe to a 45 degree bevel and lock it there, then let go of the saw.
context: Carpenters (889,700 US jobs in 2025, SOC 47-2031; BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook) cut bevels with a jigsaw on trim, stair parts, countertop and cabinet work, and set the shoe's angle before each such cut; a jigsaw is also one of the most common household power tools. On this saw (the maker's manual) the shoe sits in a 0 degree positive stop: with the bevel lever out it still will not tilt until it is slid forward off the stop. It then tilts through detents at 15, 30 and 45 degrees, and the lever pushed back under the body clamps it. A shoe left unclamped moves during the cut; one tilted only to the first detent cuts a 15 degree bevel.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midpoint between them, z up from the bench top (arm bases at y +305 and -305). A rubber bench mat 3 mm thick, fixed, x 15 to 375, y -140 to 180. On it, loose, a DeWalt DCS331 20V MAX jigsaw, bare tool: battery removed, no blade, 2.45 kg, 286 mm long. It lies on its left side with its length along x, front (blade end) away from the robot, shoe toward the robot's right and top handle toward its left; the motor housing (99 mm across) rests on the mat. The shoe is a steel plate 170 x 90 mm, 4 mm thick with a 6 mm rib 10 mm deep along both long edges (the edge is 10 mm across), standing upright: its working face is the plane y -60, its top edge 97.5 mm above the bench, its front 40 mm ahead of the gear housing (x 335). The blade line, about which the shoe tilts, is at x 275, 52.5 above the bench. The bevel lever lies flush in the gap between shoe and motor housing (y -48 to -42), pivot at x 180, with a finger tab at its rear end (x 123 to 133) standing 11 mm proud of the housing's upper side. Start: shoe square (0 degrees) in its 0 degree positive stop, lever flush, clamped. How it works (the maker's manual): the lever swings out to unlock (here up, to 60 degrees; it rests out once past 25 and falls flush below 25); the shoe will not tilt until it is slid forward off the stop (6 mm here; the slot allows 10); it then tilts either way to 45 degrees with detents at 15, 30 and 45; pushing the lever back under the body (within 10 degrees of flush) clamps the shoe where it is. Nothing else is on the bench.
scoring: Read every step from the saw's pose, its shoe and lever, and both grippers (real trial: protractor, ruler, spring scale, top and side video). Bevel: the shoe's angle to square, either way. Clamped: the lever within 10 degrees of flush under the body; then a 5 N push on the shoe's top edge (spring scale) moves the angle under 1 degree, against 10 degrees or more unclamped. Hands off: on every step of the last 2 s both grippers (every part of the fingers) at least 5 cm from the saw. Still: over those 2 s the bevel changes 0.5 degree or less, the lever 2 degrees or less and the body 2 mm or less. Unlocked off the stop: at some point the lever is out (10 degrees or more) while the shoe is 6 mm or more forward of its 0 degree stop (a mark on the shoe against the gear housing). 1.0: hands off, still, bevel 45 +-2 degrees and clamped. 0.75: hands off, still, bevel 45 +-2 degrees, not clamped. 0.5: hands off, still, bevel 28 degrees or more (the 30 detent or past it) but not 45 +-2. 0.25: unlocked off the stop at some point, and none of the above (a held shoe, a shoe at 15, a saw still being touched). 0 otherwise. 0 for the rest of the trial if the saw is pushed 30 mm or more from where it lay (tape marks), turned 15 degrees or more up off its side, or dropped. Doing nothing scores 0. The trial ends once 1.0 has held 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the lever out, tilt the shoe back to 0, slide it back into the 0 degree stop and push the lever back under the body; check the shoe will not tilt. Battery out, no blade. Lay the saw on its left side on the mat on its tape marks: front away from the robot, shoe toward the robot's right, its working face on the line y -60, blade line at x 275.
fidelity: One software rule: stop, detents and clamp are joint drive targets (clamped: stiff, 5 N on the edge turns it 0.6 deg; free: slide and tilt follow the hand, tilt held at 0 until 6 mm forward, detents pull 0.03 N m; lever over-centre 0.05 N m). Rigid boxes; shoe and lever do not collide with the body. 5.4 lb, length and width from retailer listings. Estimates: shoe and lever sizes and masses, the 6 mm stop and 10 mm slot, all forces, the handle's shape.
